entries.classDescription: Monoterpene; the most abundant terpene in modern commercial cannabis.
entries.mechanism: Often described as mildly sedating and muscle-relaxing in patient reports. Binds to several non-cannabinoid receptors in vitro; in-vivo effects in humans are not well quantified.

entries.classDescription: Monoterpene; the second most abundant terpene in many strains.
entries.mechanism: Studied for mood-elevating and anxiolytic effects in small human and animal studies. The mechanism likely involves serotonin receptor modulation and increased adenosine signaling rather than direct cannabinoid-receptor binding.

sources.label: PubMed: Limonene — anxiolytic and antidepressant-like effects (animal models)

entries.classDescription: Sesquiterpene; the only terpene known to also act as a dietary cannabinoid (CB2 agonist).
entries.mechanism: Binds directly to the CB2 cannabinoid receptor in vitro. Studied in animal models for anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects; human clinical data is limited.

entries.classDescription: Monoterpene alcohol; a common sedative and anxiolytic in aromatherapy research.
entries.mechanism: Modulates GABA-A receptor activity (similar to some anxiolytics) and inhibits glutamate release in animal models. Studied for anti-anxiety and sedative effects, primarily via inhalation (aromatherapy) rather than oral.

entries.classDescription: Monoterpene; the most common terpene in nature and the namesake of pine trees.
entries.mechanism: Studied as a bronchodilator in human and animal models. In vitro evidence suggests it may counteract some short-term memory impairment associated with THC, though this is not established in clinical trials.

entries.classDescription: Monoterpene; less common in modern commercial cannabis but characteristic of a few classic strains.
entries.aroma: Floral, herbal, piney, with a slightly sweet citrus edge.
entries.mechanism: Studied in vitro for antioxidant and mildly sedative properties; in-vivo human data is limited. Often associated with uplifting or mildly sedative subjective effects in patient reports.

entries.classDescription: Monoterpene; common in aromatic herbs and many cannabis strains in trace amounts.
entries.aroma: Sweet, herbal, woody, with a tropical fruit edge.
entries.mechanism: Studied in vitro for anti-inflammatory and decongestant activity. No clinical trials in cannabis users; subjective effects in patients are not well characterized.

entries.classDescription: Sesquiterpene; namesake of hops and a common minor terpene in cannabis.
entries.mechanism: Studied in animal models for anti-inflammatory activity and as an appetite suppressant (contrasts with THC's appetite-stimulating effect). Human clinical evidence is limited.

entries.classDescription: Sesquiterpene alcohol; common in chamomile and several cannabis cultivars.
entries.mechanism: Studied in vitro for anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and skin-soothing effects. Used in cosmetic formulations as a delivery enhancer; subjective cannabis effects are not well characterized.
Studied in vitro for anti-inflammatory activity. In-vivo data is limited; patient reports are sparse.

entries.classDescription: Monoterpene alcohol; common in rose, geranium, and several cannabis cultivars.
entries.mechanism: Studied in vitro for anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective, and antioxidant activity. Limited in-vivo data; not widely studied in cannabis users.

entries.classDescription: Monoterpene ether; dominant in eucalyptus and a minor terpene in some cannabis strains.
entries.mechanism: Studied in human trials (outside cannabis) as a bronchodilator and mild anti-inflammatory. In cannabis, subjective effects are reported as cooling and clarifying but are not well characterized in clinical literature.
